import pytest
if pytest.use_correct:
    from correct_python_programs.lcs_length import lcs_length
else:
    from python_programs.lcs_length import lcs_length


def test_attack_1():
    # identical strings require diagonal propagation (kills dp[i-1,j] bug)
    assert lcs_length("abc", "abc") == 3
    assert lcs_length("ab", "ab") == 2


def test_attack_2():
    # substring vs subsequence: subsequence would be 3
    assert lcs_length("abcde", "ace") == 1


def test_attack_3():
    # substring vs subsequence: subsequence would be 3 (abd / acd)
    assert lcs_length("abcd", "acbd") == 1


def test_attack_4():
    # empty inputs
    assert lcs_length("", "abc") == 0
    assert lcs_length("abc", "") == 0
    assert lcs_length("", "") == 0


def test_attack_5():
    # no common characters
    assert lcs_length("abc", "def") == 0
    assert lcs_length("a", "b") == 0


def test_attack_6():
    # docstring examples
    assert lcs_length("witch", "sandwich") == 2
    assert lcs_length("meow", "homeowner") == 4


def test_attack_7():
    # repeats / overlap, limited by shorter string
    assert lcs_length("aaaa", "aa") == 2
    assert lcs_length("ababa", "baba") == 4
    assert lcs_length("a", "a") == 1


def test_attack_8():
    # middle substring and symmetry
    assert lcs_length("abcdef", "zabxy") == 2
    assert lcs_length("zabxy", "abcdef") == 2
    assert lcs_length("xyzabcq", "123abc456") == 3
